title_en: Rethinking Reasoning Effort Training in Large Language Models: On-Policy Distillation or Reinforcement Learning?
title_zh: 重新审视大语言模型中的推理努力训练：同策略蒸馏还是强化学习？
summary_en: This paper systematically compares reinforcement learning (RL) and on-policy distillation (OPD) for controlling reasoning effort in large language models. Length-penalized RL reliably compresses a single policy, cutting AIME25 thinking by 70% without accuracy loss, but collapses effort tiers when trained jointly. Multi-teacher OPD separates tiers: across 33 benchmarks, low and medium tiers use 58% and 43% fewer thinking tokens than high, while high improves over the reference policy by 3.1 points. The authors attribute this to the training signal: sequence-level rewards cannot distinguish tier-specific from shared behavior, whereas OPD provides a tier-specific target at every visited state, including the stop decision. They further show a single token-level KL anchor on the high tier suffices to learn separated tiers within one RL stage, and that natural-language effort instructions make separation emerge from the start of training, matching multi-teacher OPD at equal thinking length. However, the separation built by dense targets holds only on training-seen states and does not transfer to unseen agentic tasks.
summary_zh: 本文系统比较了强化学习（RL）与同策略蒸馏（OPD）在控制大语言模型推理努力方面的效果。带长度惩罚的 RL 能可靠压缩单一策略，在 AIME25 上减少 70% 思考量且不损失准确率，但联合训练多个努力层级时会导致层级坍缩。多教师 OPD 则能分离层级：在 33 个基准上，低、中层级比高层级分别少用 58% 和 43% 的思考 token，同时高层级较参考策略提升 3.1 分。作者将差异归因于训练信号：序列级奖励无法区分层级特定行为与共享行为，而 OPD 在每个访问状态（包括停止决策）提供层级特定目标。进一步表明，仅在高层级加一个 token 级 KL 锚点即可在单阶段 RL 中学习分离层级，且自然语言努力指令能让分离从训练初期就出现，在相同思考长度下达到与多教师 OPD 竞争的策略。但由稠密目标建立的分离仅在训练见过的状态上有效，无法迁移到未见过的智能体任务。
content_en: Large language models have shown strong capabilities on complex tasks, yet how to control their reasoning effort remains a significant challenge for practical deployment. This paper provides a systematic investigation of reasoning-effort training, contrasting reinforcement learning (RL) with on-policy distillation (OPD). We find that compressing reasoning and separating effort tiers are governed by different signals. Length-penalized RL reliably compresses a single policy, reducing thinking on AIME25 by 70\% without accuracy loss, but collapses the tiers when they are trained jointly. Multi-teacher OPD separates them: across 33 benchmarks, low and medium use 58\% and 43\% fewer thinking tokens than high, while high improves on the reference policy by 3.1 points. We trace this difference to the training signal. A sequence-level reward cannot tell tier-specific behavior from shared behavior, whereas OPD supplies a tier-specific target at every visited state, including the decision to stop.
